correctness.rationale: All quantifiers n>=2 and arbitrary nonzero real coefficients are explicit. Value-swap involution rigorously gives Cov(D_i,E_j)=1/[2n(n-1)]; local three-rank enumeration gives tridiagonal marginal covariance. Positive-definite Cauchy-Schwarz and the exactly solved Dirichlet recurrence yield the unique sharp optimizer, linear projection, finite exceptional cases, and asymptotic 6/n. The standalone standard-library script exhaustively checks all permutations for n=2..8 and 497 rational identities; infinite proof is analytic, not inferred from finite checks.

originality.rationale: The reviewed claim is the evaluated sharp arbitrary-weight linear cross-correlation of the two local descent profiles, with unique optimizer/projection and exact finite boundary effects. Earlier aggregate two-sided Eulerian counts and scalar total covariance, along with Foulkes's full joint descent-composition enumeration, are acknowledged as prior and excluded from novelty. Full-text comparisons and related published claims found no displayed optimal-weight theorem, although implicit derivability from Foulkes and unavailable full texts of some relevant published results are real priority risks.

value.rationale: The finding solves a natural extremal dependence question for two competing local order representations of a random ranking, not merely a marginal moment. It identifies the complete rank-one cross-covariance, a universal zero-sum orthogonality, the exact common best linear predictor of every inverse-descent event, and the unique nonconstant boundary-layer optimal weighting. The exact asymptotic decorrelation rate 6/n and the finite-size exceptions are substantive structural information for two-sided rank statistics.
